extractedFrom: 56 Gemini CLI session documents, 6391 messages, SALT-NLP/SWE-chat
note: Gemini CLI is not JSONL. The whole file is one JSON document, normally {sessionId, projectHash, startTime, lastUpdated, messages, kind} though one of the 56 measured is a bare {messages} with no session wrapper at all, so a reader cannot assume the header exists. Each message is {id, timestamp, type, content, thoughts, tokens, model, toolCalls} and `type` is the only discriminator in the format, which is why recordTypes is the ONLY vocabulary this file ships. There are no content blocks: `content` is a plain string, and the other payload-bearing parts of a message (thoughts, toolCalls, displayContent) are FIELDS, not a type-tagged union. Field-level retention is not the schema's job in this design, it is the reader's, exactly as PROSE_FIELDS in records.mjs governs which fields of a kept Claude Code record survive; so contentBlocks, attachmentTypes and systemSubtypes are all absent rather than empty, and what those fields hold is recorded under findings for the reader PR instead of being smuggled in here as fake block names. Nothing is mapped onto another harness: `gemini` is not `assistant`, and the collision reported between this harness and a Claude Code type is addressed under findings.

rationale.recordTypes.gemini: 5647 messages, 1607094 bytes of string content across 4660 distinct openings. The agent's prose, and after the finding on `user` below it is very nearly the only prose this harness preserves.
rationale.recordTypes.user: 603 messages and only 14922 bytes of content, which is the measurement that matters here: 573 of the 603 hold the literal string [object Object], or a comma-joined run of them. Gemini CLI stringified an object array into a string field and destroyed the user's own words before deident ever saw the log. Thirty messages survive with real prose, 5143 bytes in total. Kept without hesitation, because those thirty are the highest-value records in the corpus, but nobody should read a Gemini export as a record of what the user asked.
rationale.recordTypes.info: 118 messages, 3661 bytes, and only 18 distinct strings across all of them. Harness status notices: request cancelled, loop detection disabled, a compress-threshold notice, a prohibited-content stop. Markers, written by the tool about itself.
rationale.recordTypes.warning: 14 messages, 1540 bytes, ONE distinct string across all 14: a named hook failing for an event, with a keypress hint. A marker, and the one string names a third-party hook.
rationale.recordTypes.error: 9 messages, 828 bytes, 6 distinct strings. MCP discovery and transport failures naming servers, and an API quota message. Vendor error text about the tool's own plumbing, not about the work; the Claude Code side drops raw stderr for the same reason.

findings.thoughtsAreNotEmpty: Checked rather than assumed, and the answer is the opposite of the Claude Code precedent. Claude Code writes thinking as an empty string and keeps only an encrypted signature; 7771 blocks measured there were empty at 0 bytes. Gemini CLI's `thoughts` is an array of {subject, description, timestamp} carrying real, discursive agent prose: 2385 messages carry them, 4252 entries in total, 1418109 bytes of subject and description text, and NOT ONE of the 4252 is empty. That is close to the weight of `content` itself and it is the single largest block of prose in the corpus after content. It is a field, so it gets no vocabulary entry, but a reader that keeps a `gemini` record and copies its fields through will ship 1.4 MB of reasoning prose per corpus of this size, and the redaction pass has to cover it.
findings.toolCallsCarryTheirResults: `toolCalls` is an array of {id, name, args, result, resultDisplay, status, timestamp, displayName, description, renderOutputAsMarkdown} hanging off the message, so Gemini CLI merges the call and its output into the record rather than emitting a separate result record. The weight is the finding: 5234 calls across 5114 messages, 4481768 bytes of args against 89763149 bytes of result and resultDisplay. That is 89 MB of tool output against 1.6 MB of content, a ratio of roughly 55 to 1, and it is by far the largest retention question this harness poses. Statuses measured: success 4958, error 232, cancelled 44. Tool names measured: run_shell_command 1685, replace 1276, read_file 811, write_file 483, grep_search 89. Whoever writes the reader must decide `result` and `resultDisplay` explicitly; keeping the message and copying its fields ships the lot.
findings.displayContentIsToolOutput: 24 messages carry a `displayContent` field, and every one of them is on a `user`-typed message. The content measured is not user text at all: it is functionResponse objects holding tool output, including absolute paths under the account's home directory and the modified file body inline. A reader that treats a user record as user prose and copies its fields will ship tool output through the one record type nobody would think to check.
findings.noFileHistorySnapshot: The brief for this work reported that Gemini CLI emits a top-level file-history-snapshot record sharing a name with a Claude Code type, and said to decide it on Gemini's own evidence. Gemini's own evidence is that it does not exist. The transcript directory held 58 files, of which 2 are Claude Code JSONL transcripts misfiled into it (they open with parentUuid and isSidechain, and one begins with a Claude Code summary record). file-history-snapshot appears in those 2 files and in no Gemini document. The 56 real Gemini documents carry exactly seven top-level keys: messages, sessionId, projectHash, startTime, lastUpdated, kind, summary. There is no name collision to resolve, so no decision is recorded for it: an undecided name refuses, which is the right outcome if a later corpus proves otherwise.
findings.sessionHeaderUndecided: The document-level keys are not typed records and have no entries here. They hold sessionId, projectHash, startTime, lastUpdated, `kind` which read main in all 47 documents that carry it, and `summary`, present on 14 documents, which is a one-line written description of the session such as a roadmap-update title. projectHash is a stable per-project identifier and summary is prose; both need a decision in the reader PR. This key is prose for a human; the loader reads only the four decision sections and ignores it.
